source.citation: Balazi, Allaire, Jolivet and Omnes (2025), Numer. Methods Partial Differential Equations 41(6), e70057
source.question: Appendix A: existence of a quintic enrichment Sigma_5(K) for the fourth-order space V_4(K) (n=3)

claims.statement: For every n>=1 the face (P_n) and cell (P_(n-1)) moment map M_n is injective on P_(n+1), has a 7-dimensional kernel on P_(n+2) spanned by four vertex Jacobi ridges and three pair Legendre ridges, rank C(n+5,3)-7, deficit (n-1)(n-2)/2, and is surjective on P_(n+3).
Minimum degree of a single-cell polynomial space containing P_(n+1) unisolvent for M_n: n+2 for n=1,2; n+3 for n>=3.
For n=3 the alternating face functional A vanishes on P_5 and A(Delta_4)=1/34650; no 15-dimensional quintic enrichment of P_4 exists.
Every admissible space has at least (n-1)(n-2)/2 directions outside P_(n+2); vertex-invariant spaces attaining this exist for every n.
The missing directions form sgn x Sym^(n-3)(std) of S_4.
P_(n+2)+Delta_4 P_(n-3) gives a lean element for n=3..8; explicit n=4 and n=5 elements.
Delta_4 P_(n-3) is a lean enrichment for every n.
V_3^* = (a_B-orthogonal complement of the ridges in P_5) + span{Delta_4} has dimension 50, contains P_4, is unisolvent and vertex-invariant; 14-monomial basis.
Kernel dimension sum_(r=1)^min(d,n+2) C(d,r); closed-form deficit zero exactly when d=2 or n<=2; triangles never need extra degree; minimum degree between n+3 and n+d for d>=3, n>=3.
M_(d,n) surjective on P_(n+3) for d=4 (n<=5), d=5 (n<=4), d=6 (n=3).
Degree n+3 suffices on every d-simplex, d>=4.

V_3^* with discontinuous P_3 pressure on Kuhn meshes: rates consistent with fourth-order convergence (N=5: 3.90 broken H1 velocity, 4.89 L2 velocity, 4.04 pressure); computed discrete inf-sup values 0.4017, 0.3817, 0.3743, 0.3702 for N=1..4.

exclusions: No minimum-degree assertion for split-cell, nonpolynomial or virtual element spaces, or for all Stokes elements.
No pointwise divergence-free or pressure-robustness assertion.
No p-uniform stability, curved-element result, discrete Korn inequality or solver-speed claim.
